subject: Re-anchor request: MAP adjustments + procurement bridge
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeinc.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Lindstrom <markus.lindstrom@acmeinc.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Need to re-anchor MAP — evaluation delays on our side

Mateo,

Quick note from our end — the internal evaluation gate at Acme hit two blockers this week: the security team needs the live SOC2 evidence (they flagged a logging nuance) and our data infra team has delayed access to the test VPC until next week. Between the two we now expect a 10–14 day push on the original acceptance schedule unless we re-scope.

Attached is an updated evaluation checklist showing which tests can be executed without the VPC access. Can Redwood pivot to a staged MAP so we can validate key functionality first and defer the network-bound cases?

Our asks:
- A two-phase MAP that lets us sign off on UI/semantic tests by Sept 17 and full end-to-end by Sept 30.
- Temporary hold on the final PO deadline; procurement needs dates to align with the acceptance signoff.
- A short-term SLA commitment for dedicated capacity for the first phase (we're in a tight pilot window).

Appreciate a proposed route and whether Redwood can cover a short credit/hold if procurement slips.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Director, Product Evaluation
Acme Inc

Attachment: ACME_eval_checklist_v2.xlsx
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-29T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Need to re-anchor MAP — evaluation delays on our side

Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the checklist. We've reviewed the attachment and we can absolutely split the MAP into two milestones. Proposal below (high level):

Phase A (low-friction, Sept 14–17 window)
- Priority: UI/semantic correctness, response quality, basic throughput (no VPC required)
- Redwood deliverables: hosted model variant, a reserved burst slot, & a test harness with golden prompts
- Acceptance: signoff on 5 canonical prompt sets in the checklist

Phase B (end-to-end, Sept 28–30 window)
- Priority: VPC tests, KV/streamed-input flows, and audit/logging checks
- Redwood deliverables: private deployment snapshot, SOC2 evidence pointers, and a temporary dedicated pool for the run

Notes/asks for Acme:
1) Please confirm which checklist items you want in Phase A (we highlighted candidates in MAP_v3.pdf).
2) Procurement: we can hold a modest provisional capacity (no charge) for two weeks after the Phase A window to avoid cutover friction — we request a PO commitment date by Sept 3 to guarantee Phase B capacity.

I'll attach a tracked MAP (MAP_v3.pdf) with milestone owners and clear acceptance criteria. Laura — can you help draft the procurement bridge terms and confirm whether we can offer the two-week provisional hold? Rishi — can you validate the SOC2 evidence we can package quickly?

Elena, if those dates look reasonable we'll treat this as an official re-anchor and update the HubSpot timeline. If Acme prefers a later Phase A, give two proposed windows and we'll re-provision.

Regards,
Mateo
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP_v3.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeinc.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Need to re-anchor MAP — procurement bridge thought

Circling with procurement notes from my call with Markus this morning. He confirmed Acme's legal can sign quickly but the PO timeline is the gating item — internal approvals target a PO by Sept 3, not Sept 10 as originally thought. Good news but short runway.

We should do the following:
- Offer a formal one-time provisional hold for two weeks at zero charge to avoid losing Phase A capacity. Contract team can issue a short addendum rather than a full SOW overhaul.
- Offer a small usage credit (one-time) if PO + final acceptance slip beyond Sept 10 (this is a lever to keep momentum).
- I drafted bridge terms (procurement_bridge_terms.docx) that list the holding mechanics and liability language — please review.

Risks to flag in the MAP update:
1) If SOC2 evidence cannot be produced within 7 business days, Phase B acceptance is at risk.
2) If procurement delays beyond Sept 10 we expose dedicated pool to reallocation — we will attempt to reserve but cannot guarantee beyond two weeks without revenue commitment.

I'll prepare a short exec summary for Grace if we need a credit approval. Mateo, please confirm you want me to loop her.

-Laura
Sr. Sales Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

On Fri, Aug 29, 2026 at 10:02 Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-31T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: approval request for credit + SLA exception (Acme / ACME-4821)

Grace — quick escalation and recommended decision points. Context: Acme requested a two-phase MAP after internal evaluation blockers. Procurement is likely to deliver PO by Sept 3, but there is a non-zero chance it slides. To preserve timeline and avoid losing momentum we can do a short bridge as Laura suggests; that requires one-time approvals:

Approval asks:
- One-time usage credit (estimate: $2,500) if PO misses the Sept 10 soft cutoff.
- SLA exception to reserve a dedicated burst pool for Phase A (up to two weeks).

Attached is a two-line risk log excerpt to put this in the decision record: 
- Risk: SOC2 evidence delay — Impact: Phase B failure — Mitigation: bundle available evidence + prioritized audit appendix; contingency: defer Phase B to Sept 30.
- Risk: Procurement slip — Impact: capacity reallocation — Mitigation: two-week provisional hold, one-time credit.

If you OK both items I'll route a short approval email and Laura will issue the procurement addendum. If you want tighter controls we can require a signed MSA amendment before hold is applied (slower).

Recommend: Approve credit + hold to maintain customer momentum.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, GTM Strategy, Redwood Inference
